questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. # MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Base directory for this skill: /home/claude/.claude-switch/accounts/main/skills/caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE once triggered. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only when user says "stop caveman" or "normal mode".

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Abbreviate common terms (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl). Strip conjunctions. Use arrows for causality (X -> Y). One word when one word enough.

Technical terms stay exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

### Examples

**"Why React component re-render?"**

> Inline obj prop -> new ref -> re-render. `useMemo`.

**"Explain database connection pooling."**

> Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake -> fast under load.

## Auto-Clarity Exception

Drop caveman temporarily for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example -- destructive op:

> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
>
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
>
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

# Pennywise

I keep my household money in a plain text file and I'm tired of spreadsheets. I'd like a small
Python tool called **pennywise** that reads that file and tells me where the money went. It should
work two ways: as a library I can `import pennywise` from my own scripts, and as a `pennywise`
command I run in the terminal. Python 3.9 or newer, standard library only (no third-party
packages). Running `pip install .` in the project folder should give me both the importable
library and the `pennywise` command.

## The ledger file

One entry per line:

```
# household, March
2024-03-01 salary 2500.00 March pay
2024-03-02 groceries -42.50 weekly shop

2024-03-05 Rent -900
```

Each line has a date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), a category (one word), an amount, and an optional note. The
fields are separated by any amount of spaces or tabs. The note is the rest of the line exactly as I
wrote it (it can contain spaces), apart from trimming whitespace at both ends.

- A positive amount is money in, a negative one is money out. The sign is optional for money in, so
  `2500`, `+2500` and `2500.00` are all the same. Amounts have at most two decimal places: `12`,
  `12.5`, `-0.99` are fine; `12.505`, `1,000.00` and `abc` are not.
- Categories do not care about case: `Rent` and `rent` are the same category, and it is shown in
  lower case.
- Blank lines are ignored, and so are lines starting with `#`.
- Anything else is a mistake in my file, and the tool must tell me which line (counting from 1,
  blank and comment lines included). A date that does not exist, like `2024-02-30`, is a mistake
  too.

## Using it as a library

```python
import pennywise

entries = pennywise.parse(open("house.txt").read())
print(pennywise.balance(entries))
```

- `parse(text)` returns a list of entries, in the order they appear. Each entry has `.date` (a
  `datetime.date`), `.category` (a lower-case `str`), `.amount` (a `decimal.Decimal`) and `.note`
  (a `str`, empty when there is none).
- A bad line makes `parse` raise `pennywise.ParseError`. It is a `ValueError`, its `.line`
  attribute is the line number, and its message mentions `line N`.
- `balance(entries)` is the total of all amounts, a `Decimal` (zero for no entries).
- `by_category(entries)` is a `dict` of category to its total; `by_month(entries)` is the same
  keyed by month, like `"2024-03"`.
- `filter_entries(entries, category=None, since=None, until=None)` returns the matching entries in
  the order given. `category` is matched without regard to case; `since` and `until` are
  `datetime.date` values and both ends are included. Anything left as `None` is not filtered on.

## Using it from the terminal

content.content:
$ pennywise balance house.txt
1457.50

$ pennywise summary house.txt
groceries  -42.50
rent  -900.00
salary  2500.00

$ pennywise list house.txt --category groceries
2024-03-02 groceries -42.50 weekly shop
```

- `pennywise balance FILE` prints the total with two decimals, on one line.
- `pennywise summary FILE [--by category|month]` prints one line per group, sorted by name: the
  name, some spaces, then the total with two decimals. The default is `--by category`.
- `pennywise list FILE [--category C] [--since DATE] [--until DATE]` prints the matching entries,
  oldest first (entries on the same day keep the order of the file), one per line as
  `DATE CATEGORY AMOUNT NOTE`. The amount always has two decimals, and the note (and the space
  before it) is left out when there is none.
- `pennywise add FILE DATE CATEGORY AMOUNT [NOTE]` adds an entry to the end of the file (creating
  the file if it does not exist) and prints the line it added, written the same way `list` writes
  it. I pass the note as a single quoted argument. An invalid entry is refused and the file is left
  exactly as it was.
- `pennywise export FILE [--format csv]` prints the entries, in the same order as `list`, as CSV
  with the header `date,category,amount,note`. CSV is the only format for now and the default.
- `balance`, `summary` and `list` take `--json` to print JSON instead. Amounts are strings with two
  decimals: `{"balance": "1457.50"}`, `{"groceries": "-42.50", "rent": "-900.00"}`, and for `list`
  an array of `{"date": "2024-03-02", "category": "groceries", "amount": "-42.50", "note":
  "weekly shop"}`.
- Wherever a command reads a file (not `add`), `-` means read the ledger from standard input.
- Exit status: `0` when it worked; `1` when the ledger (or the entry given to `add`) has a mistake,
  with a message on standard error that names the line and nothing on standard output; `2` when
  the file cannot be read or the command line is wrong (no command, an unknown command, a bad
  option value, a date I mistyped).
"""Command-line interface."""

import argparse
import json
import sys
from typing import List, Optional

from . import ledger


class _ReadError(Exception):
    pass


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="pennywise")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True, metavar="COMMAND")

    p_balance = sub.add_parser("balance", help="print the total of all entries")
    p_balance.add_argument("file", metavar="FILE", help="ledger file, or - for stdin")
    p_balance.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print JSON")
    p_balance.set_defaults(handler=_cmd_balance)

    p_summary = sub.add_parser("summary", help="print totals per category or month")
    p_summary.add_argument("file", metavar="FILE", help="ledger file, or - for stdin")
    p_summary.add_argument(
        "--by", choices=("category", "month"), default="category",
        help="group by category (default) or month",
    )
    p_summary.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print JSON")
    p_summary.set_defaults(handler=_cmd_summary)
    return parser


def _read_ledger(path: str) -> str:
    try:
        if path == "-":
            stream = sys.stdin
            raw = getattr(stream, "buffer", None)
            if raw is None:
                return stream.read()
            return raw.read().decode("utf-8")
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            return handle.read().decode("utf-8")
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
        raise _ReadError("cannot read %s: %s" % (path, exc)) from None


def _cmd_balance(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    entries = ledger.parse(_read_ledger(args.file))
    total = ledger.format_amount(ledger.balance(entries))
    if args.json:
        return json.dumps({"balance": total})
    return total


def _cmd_summary(args: argparse.Namespace) -> Optional[str]:
    entries = ledger.parse(_read_ledger(args.file))
    group = ledger.by_month if args.by == "month" else ledger.by_category
    totals = {k: ledger.format_amount(v) for k, v in sorted(group(entries).items())}
    if args.json:
        return json.dumps(totals, sort_keys=True)
    if not totals:
        return None
    return "\n".join("%s  %s" % item for item in totals.items())


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    parser = _build_parser()
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    except SystemExit as exc:
        code = exc.code
        return code if isinstance(code, int) else (0 if code is None else 2)
    try:
        output = args.handler(args)
    except ledger.ParseError as exc:
        print("pennywise: %s" % exc, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except _ReadError as exc:
        print("pennywise: %s" % exc, file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if output is not None:
        print(output)
    return 0
"""pennywise: read a plain-text household ledger."""

from .ledger import (
    Entry,
    ParseError,
    balance,
    by_category,
    by_month,
    format_amount,
    parse,
)

__all__ = [
    "Entry",
    "ParseError",
    "balance",
    "by_category",
    "by_month",
    "format_amount",
    "parse",
]

import datetime
import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from tests import _path  # noqa: F401
import pennywise
from pennywise import Entry, ParseError, balance, by_category, by_month, format_amount, parse

EXAMPLE = """# household, March
2024-03-01 salary 2500.00 March pay
2024-03-02 groceries -42.50 weekly shop

2024-03-05 Rent -900
"""


class ParseExampleTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_example_ledger(self):
        entries = parse(EXAMPLE)
        self.assertEqual(len(entries), 3)
        self.assertEqual(
            entries[0],
            Entry(datetime.date(2024, 3, 1), "salary", Decimal("2500.00"), "March pay"),
        )
        self.assertEqual(entries[1].note, "weekly shop")
        self.assertEqual(entries[2].category, "rent")
        self.assertEqual(entries[2].note, "")
        self.assertIsInstance(entries[2].date, datetime.date)
        self.assertIsInstance(entries[2].amount, Decimal)

    def test_public_api_reexported(self):
        self.assertIs(pennywise.parse, parse)
        self.assertIs(pennywise.Entry, Entry)
        self.assertIs(pennywise.ParseError, ParseError)
        self.assertIs(pennywise.balance, balance)

    def test_entry_is_frozen_with_default_note(self):
        e = Entry(datetime.date(2024, 1, 1), "x", Decimal(1))
        self.assertEqual(e.note, "")
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            e.note = "changed"


class AmountTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def amount(self, text):
        return parse("2024-01-01 x " + text)[0].amount

    def test_valid_amounts(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.amount("12"), Decimal("12"))
        self.assertEqual(self.amount("12.5"), Decimal("12.5"))
        self.assertEqual(self.amount("-0.99"), Decimal("-0.99"))
        self.assertEqual(self.amount("+2500"), Decimal("2500"))
        self.assertEqual(self.amount("2500.00"), Decimal("2500.00"))

    def test_invalid_amounts(self):
        for bad in ["12.505", "1,000.00", "abc", ".5", "12.", "--1", "1e3", "١٢"]:
            with self.subTest(bad=bad):
                with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
                    parse("2024-01-01 x " + bad)
                self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 1)

    def test_error_message_format(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
            parse("\n\n2024-01-01 x abc")
        self.assertEqual(str(ctx.exception), "line 3: invalid amount 'abc'")


class DateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_bad_dates(self):
        for bad in ["2024-02-30", "2024-13-01", "24-01-01", "2024/01/01", "2024-1-1", "xxxx-xx-xx"]:
            with self.subTest(bad=bad):
                with self.assertRaises(ParseError):
                    parse(bad + " x 1")

    def test_leap_day(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse("2024-02-29 x 1")[0].date, datetime.date(2024, 2, 29))


class ParseErrorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_is_value_error_with_line(self):
        err = ParseError(7, "boom")
        self.assertIsInstance(err, ValueError)
        self.assertEqual(err.line, 7)
        self.assertEqual(str(err), "line 7: boom")

    def test_line_counts_blank_and_comment_lines(self):
        text = "# c\n\n   \n2024-01-01 a 1\n# c\nbad line here\n"
        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
            parse(text)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 6)
        self.assertIn("line 6", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_too_few_fields(self):
        for bad in ["2024-01-01", "2024-01-01 food"]:
            with self.subTest(bad=bad):
                with self.assertRaises(ParseError):
                    parse(bad)


class WhitespaceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_tabs_and_spaces_between_fields(self):
        e = parse("2024-01-01\t\tfood \t 5.00\t lunch  with\t bob  ")[0]
        self.assertEqual(e.category, "food")
        self.assertEqual(e.amount, Decimal("5.00"))
        self.assertEqual(e.note, "lunch  with\t bob")

    def test_leading_whitespace_and_indented_comment(self):
        entries = parse("   2024-01-01 a 1\n  \t# note\n\t\n")
        self.assertEqual(len(entries), 1)

    def test_crlf(self):
        entries = parse("2024-01-01 a 1 hi\r\n\r\n2024-01-02 b 2\r\n")
        self.assertEqual([e.note for e in entries], ["hi", ""])

    def test_empty_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse(""), [])


class BalanceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_empty(self):
        result = balance([])
        self.assertEqual(result, Decimal(0))
        self.assertIsInstance(result, Decimal)

    def test_example(self):
        self.assertEqual(balance(parse(EXAMPLE)), Decimal("1557.50"))

    def test_decimal_exact(self):
        entries = parse("2024-01-01 a 0.10\n2024-01-01 a 0.20\n")
        self.assertEqual(balance(entries), Decimal("0.30"))


class FormatAmountTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_formats(self):
        self.assertEqual(format_amount(Decimal("1457.5")), "1457.50")
        self.assertEqual(format_amount(Decimal("-42.5")), "-42.50")
        self.assertEqual(format_amount(Decimal("+2500")), "2500.00")
        self.assertEqual(format_amount(Decimal("0")), "0.00")

    def test_never_negative_zero(self):
        self.assertEqual(format_amount(Decimal("-0.00")), "0.00")
        self.assertEqual(format_amount(Decimal("-0")), "0.00")
        self.assertEqual(format_amount(Decimal("-0.001")), "0.00")

    def test_no_exponent(self):
        self.assertEqual(format_amount(Decimal("1E+3")), "1000.00")

    def test_huge_amount(self):
        big = "9" * 40
        self.assertEqual(format_amount(Decimal(big)), big + ".00")


class GroupTotalTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_by_category_merges_case_and_keeps_first_appearance_order(self):
        entries = parse(
            "2024-03-01 Rent -900\n2024-03-02 food -5\n2024-04-01 rent -100\n2024-04-02 Food 1.5\n"
        )
        result = by_category(entries)
        self.assertIsInstance(result, dict)
        self.assertEqual(list(result.items()), [("rent", Decimal("-1000")), ("food", Decimal("-3.5"))])
        self.assertTrue(all(isinstance(v, Decimal) for v in result.values()))

    def test_by_month_keys(self):
        entries = parse("2024-03-01 a 1\n2023-12-31 a 2\n2024-03-30 b 3\n0999-01-01 c 4\n")
        result = by_month(entries)
        self.assertEqual(
            list(result.items()),
            [("2024-03", Decimal(4)), ("2023-12", Decimal(2)), ("0999-01", Decimal(4))],
        )

    def test_empty(self):
        self.assertEqual(by_category([]), {})
        self.assertEqual(by_month([]), {})

    def test_reexported(self):
        self.assertIs(pennywise.by_category, by_category)
        self.assertIs(pennywise.by_month, by_month)

        )

import contextlib
import io
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest import mock

from tests import _path
from pennywise import cli

LEDGER = (
    "# household, March\n"
    "2024-03-01 salary 2500.00 March pay\n"
    "2024-03-02 groceries -42.50 weekly shop\n"
    "\n"
    "2024-03-05 Rent -900\n"
)
# PRD example totals 1557.50; the issue's 1457.50 includes another -100 line.
HOUSE = LEDGER + "2024-03-06 misc -100\n"


class CliBase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)

    def write(self, text, name="house.txt"):
        path = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, name)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            f.write(text)
        return path

    def run_main(self, argv, stdin=None):
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        ctx = [contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err)]
        if stdin is not None:
            ctx.append(mock.patch.object(sys, "stdin", io.TextIOWrapper(io.BytesIO(stdin))))
        with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
            for c in ctx:
                stack.enter_context(c)
            code = cli.main(argv)
        return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()


class BalanceTests(CliBase):
    def test_balance(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main(["balance", self.write(HOUSE)])
        self.assertEqual((code, out, err), (0, "1457.50\n", ""))

    def test_balance_json(self):
        code, out, _ = self.run_main(["balance", self.write(HOUSE), "--json"])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (0, '{"balance": "1457.50"}\n'))

    def test_stdin(self):
        code, out, _ = self.run_main(["balance", "-"], stdin=HOUSE.encode("utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (0, "1457.50\n"))

    def test_stdin_without_buffer(self):
        out = io.StringIO()
        with mock.patch.object(sys, "stdin", io.StringIO(HOUSE)), contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
            code = cli.main(["balance", "-"])
        self.assertEqual((code, out.getvalue()), (0, "1457.50\n"))

    def test_zero_is_not_negative(self):
        path = self.write("2024-01-01 a 5\n2024-01-02 a -5\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_main(["balance", path])[1], "0.00\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_main(["balance", self.write("", "e.txt")])[1], "0.00\n")

    def test_utf8_note_and_crlf(self):
        path = self.write("2024-01-01 café 5 ☕\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_main(["balance", path])[:2], (0, "5.00\n"))


class SummaryTests(CliBase):
    def test_default_by_category(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main(["summary", self.write(LEDGER)])
        self.assertEqual((code, err), (0, ""))
        self.assertEqual(out, "groceries  -42.50\nrent  -900.00\nsalary  2500.00\n")

    def test_by_category_sorted_by_key(self):
        path = self.write("2024-01-01 zed 1\n2024-01-02 abc 2\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_main(["summary", path])[1], "abc  2.00\nzed  1.00\n")

    def test_by_month_sorted(self):
        path = self.write("2024-03-01 a 5\n2023-12-31 a 1.5\n2024-03-09 b -2\n")
        code, out, _ = self.run_main(["summary", path, "--by", "month"])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (0, "2023-12  1.50\n2024-03  3.00\n"))

    def test_json_sorted_keys(self):
        code, out, _ = self.run_main(["summary", self.write(LEDGER), "--json"])
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertEqual(
            out, '{"groceries": "-42.50", "rent": "-900.00", "salary": "2500.00"}\n'
        )

    def test_json_by_month(self):
        code, out, _ = self.run_main(
            ["summary", self.write(LEDGER), "--by", "month", "--json"]
        )
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (0, '{"2024-03": "1557.50"}\n'))

    def test_stdin(self):
        code, out, _ = self.run_main(["summary", "-"], stdin=LEDGER.encode("utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertTrue(out.startswith("groceries  -42.50\n"))

    def test_ledger_error_exit_1(self):
        path = self.write("2024-01-01 a 1\n2024-01-02 a abc\n")
        code, out, err = self.run_main(["summary", path])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (1, ""))
        self.assertIn("line 2", err)

    def test_bad_by_exit_2(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main(["summary", self.write(LEDGER), "--by", "year"])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (2, ""))
        self.assertTrue(err)

    def test_missing_file_exit_2(self):
        code, out, _ = self.run_main(["summary", os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "nope")])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (2, ""))

    def test_empty_ledger_prints_nothing(self):
        code, out, _ = self.run_main(["summary", self.write("")])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (0, ""))

    def test_empty_ledger_json(self):
        code, out, _ = self.run_main(["summary", self.write(""), "--json"])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (0, "{}\n"))


class ErrorTests(CliBase):
    def test_bad_line_exit_1(self):
        path = self.write("2024-01-01 a 1\n\n2024-01-02 a abc\n")
        code, out, err = self.run_main(["balance", path])
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertEqual(out, "")
        self.assertEqual(err, "pennywise: line 3: invalid amount 'abc'\n")

    def test_missing_file(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main(["balance", os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "nope")])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (2, ""))
        self.assertTrue(err.startswith("pennywise: "))

    def test_directory(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main(["balance", self.tmp.name])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (2, ""))
        self.assertTrue(err)

    def test_invalid_utf8(self):
        path = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "bad.txt")
        with open(path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(b"2024-01-01 a 1 \xff\xfe\n")
        code, out, err = self.run_main(["balance", path])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (2, ""))
        self.assertTrue(err.startswith("pennywise: "))

    def test_invalid_utf8_stdin(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main(["balance", "-"], stdin=b"\xff\n")
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (2, ""))

    def test_no_subcommand(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main([])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (2, ""))
        self.assertTrue(err)

    def test_unknown_subcommand(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_main(["frobnicate"])
        self.assertEqual((code, out), (2, ""))
        self.assertTrue(err)

    def test_missing_file_arg(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_main(["balance"])[0], 2)

    def test_help_exits_zero(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_main(["--help"])[0], 0)


class SubprocessTests(CliBase):
    def run_module(self, *args, stdin=None):
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=_path.SRC)
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "pennywise", *args],
            input=stdin, capture_output=True, env=env, cwd=self.tmp.name,
        )

    def test_python_dash_m(self):
        path = self.write(HOUSE)
        res = self.run_module("balance", path)
        self.assertEqual(res.returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(res.stdout, b"1457.50\n")

    def test_python_dash_m_stdin_json(self):
        res = self.run_module("balance", "-", "--json", stdin=HOUSE.encode())
        self.assertEqual((res.returncode, res.stdout), (0, b'{"balance": "1457.50"}\n'))

    def test_python_dash_m_exit_codes(self):
        bad = self.write("nonsense\n", "bad.txt")
        res = self.run_module("balance", bad)
        self.assertEqual((res.returncode, res.stdout), (1, b""))
        self.assertIn(b"pennywise: line 1:", res.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_module().returncode, 2)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_module("balance", "missing.txt").returncode, 2)
